content: Good actions give strength to ourselves and inspire good actions in others.
author: Plato
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Genuine love is not a transaction where you keep score of who gave what; it is a state of being where you extend warmth and goodwill without needing to control the other person.

Across his life and work, Plato saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. The biggest barrier to deep connection is never external; it is our own fear of rejection. We build armor around our hearts to avoid pain, but that same armor ends up locking out the warmth and intimacy we crave.
reflectionPrompt: What long-held assumption about your life or abilities is challenged by this insight?
